summary: The first fair attack on F-001: a general line-aware scribe generator (positional word tables, glyph chain, page memory, copy-and-vary — no rule names m or line endings), fitted on public Currier B pages only, lifts the line-final to mid-line m ratio to 22.1 on the practice split against the line of 10 and beats the within-line shuffle null; R-001's failure was layout-blindness, not resistance.
